sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: As of the Nov 24 close, the S&P 500 sits at 7,201, about 6.2% below its level a month ago and in the lower half of its 1-month range (high 7,744, low 6,910). The Nasdaq 100 is weaker still at 26,214, down 10.5% over the month and closer to the bottom of its range (high 29,813, low 25,029). The VIX closed at 26.4, up from 18.4 a month ago, and the Euro Stoxx 50 is down 3.4% over the last five sessions. The week carries 32 scheduled reports from S&P 500, Russell 1000 and core names, 16 of them in technology.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Mon: Oracle (ORCL US) reports into technology, whose median 3-day reaction off recent prints is about -0.1%, while Nike (NKE US) reports into consumer-cyclical at +0.3%. Tue: MongoDB (MDB US) reports alongside Okta and GitLab. Wed: AeroVironment (AVAV US) plugs into industrials, median +0.2%. Thu is the heaviest day with 13 reports, including Dollar General (DG US) in consumer-defensive (median -0.5%) and Cooper Companies (COO US) in healthcare. Nothing on this week's calendar sits in the three sectors with the largest recent moves (mining, copper, energy).

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining (+4.6% median, 229 tickers, 2,766 news items), copper (-2.5%, 6 tickers, 231 items) and energy (+2.0%, 328 tickers, 5,167 items) lead the reaction table. Mining and energy have thick news windows; copper's is thin. None of this week's scheduled reporters belong to these sectors, so treat these medians as backdrop rather than a direct read on the week's prints.
